purpose: identify what vLLM's OWN RMSNorm dispatch actually executes on this GPU/vLLM version, to determine whether a separate 'vLLM native fused RMSNorm' baseline exists to measure
method: torch.profiler over 10 real calls to vllm.ir.ops.rms_norm(x, weight, eps, None) on a (16,4096) fp16 tensor on the GTX 1650 Max-Q, 5 warmup calls excluded
finding: WARNING emitted by vLLM itself: 'Priority not set for op rms_norm, using native implementation.' Profiler confirms dispatch to the eager decomposition: vllm_ir::rms_norm (551us CPU-side incl. dispatch overhead) -> aten::mean (35.80% of CUDA time, backed by at::native::reduce_kernel) -> aten::mul (26.02%) -> aten::to/_to_copy/copy_ (20.78%, dtype casts) -> aten::pow (8.37%) -- i.e. multiple small elementwise/reduction kernels, NOT a single fused custom kernel.
conclusion: vLLM's own production RMSNorm path on this GPU/vLLM-version (0.24.0) IS the eager PyTorch decomposition baseline (Baseline A in this slice's terminology) -- there is no separate 'vLLM native fused RMSNorm' to measure as a distinct baseline C on this hardware/software combination. This is reported honestly rather than assumed.
